dashboard.label: ITSI Maintenance Window Management - Home
dashboard.description: Manage ITSI maintenance windows interactively with the itsimaintenance command.

div.p: Create, inspect, update, cancel and (optionally) delete ITSI maintenance windows directly from a search using the itsimaintenance custom command. Results appear inline so you can see success/failure per request immediately.

Safe by default: operations run in dry-run unless you set dry_run="false". Destructive delete is disabled by default. Every request is idempotent (keyed on request_id), so re-running the same request never creates duplicates.

div.pre: | makeresults | eval operation="create", request_id="CHG123", title="CHG123 - planned maintenance", object_key="<ENTITY_OR_SERVICE_KEY>", object_type="entity", start_time="<EPOCH_START>", end_time="<EPOCH_END>", dry_run="true" | itsimaintenance
div.p: or set dry_run="false" in the row. The result row returns maintenance_window_keys on success.
div.h3: 4. Cancel or delete an existing window
div.pre: | makeresults | eval operation="cancel", request_id="CHG123-cancel", maintenance_window_key="<WINDOW_KEY>" | itsimaintenance dry_run=false
div.p: delete requires enable_delete=true in itsi_maintenance.conf [safety]. Prefer cancel.

Rows sharing a request_id are grouped into one request; a group mixing entities and services is auto-split into separate windows. Timestamps must be UTC epoch seconds (or ISO-8601 with Z/offset); end_time > start_time.

search.query: | makeresults | eval operation="list", request_id="dashboard-home" | itsimaintenance | eval start=strftime(start_time,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"), end=strftime(end_time,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z") | table title maintenance_window_key start end object_count

| inputlookup operative_maintenance_log | where maintenance_object_type="entity" AND start_time<=now() AND end_time>=now() | rename maintenance_object_key as entity_key | lookup itsi_entities _key as entity_key OUTPUT title as entity_title | eval ends=strftime(end_time,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z") | table entity_title entity_key ends calendar_origin

div.p: Each result row includes result (success / failure / noop), dry_run, maintenance_window_keys (on create), and on failure a stable error_category such as:

missing_required_field, invalid_timestamp, entity_not_found, service_not_found, duplicate_request, payload_conflict, authorization_failed_403, not_found_404, conflict_409, operation_not_allowed, limit_exceeded.
Full documentation ships in the app's docs/ folder: API contract, architecture, threat model, roles, runbook, validation report and known limitations.

update performs a full replace (read-modify-write): the tool GETs the window and PUTs the complete new definition. You must supply the entire desired end-state — title, the full set of objects, start_time and end_time. Any object you leave out is removed.
div.pre: | makeresults | eval operation="update", request_id="CHG123-update-1", maintenance_window_key="<WINDOW_KEY>", title="CHG123 - planned maintenance", object_key="<ENTITY_OR_SERVICE_KEY>", object_type="entity", start_time="<EPOCH_START>", end_time="<EPOCH_END_NEW>", dry_run="true" | itsimaintenance
div.p: For a window with several objects, send one row per object, all sharing the same request_id, maintenance_window_key, title, start_time and end_time.

ul.li: Full replace — resupply all objects or they are dropped.
One object type per window (all entities or all services).
Active or future windows only — a completed window (past end_time) is blocked (operation_not_allowed).
Titles are globally unique — keep the window's own title, or a new title not used by another window (else HTTP 409).
Use a fresh request_id per change; the same id with different data is rejected as a payload conflict.

div.p: Cancel ends a window now (active → end_time=now; future → collapsed into the past). It only works on active or future windows — a window that has already finished cannot be cancelled (nothing to cancel; its objects already left maintenance at end_time).
div.pre: | makeresults | eval operation="cancel", request_id="CHG123-cancel", maintenance_window_key="<WINDOW_KEY>" | itsimaintenance dry_run=false
div.p: Check a window is still active before cancelling:
div.pre: | inputlookup operative_maintenance_log | where calendar_origin="<WINDOW_KEY>" AND end_time>=now() | stats count as still_active
div.p: Delete removes a window entirely and is disabled by default (set enable_delete=true in itsi_maintenance.conf [safety]). Prefer letting windows expire naturally via end_time; use delete only to remove a leftover record.
The same operations can run unattended on a schedule via the bundled alert action, instead of interactively with the command.

ul.li: Build a search that outputs the window-definition rows (same field contract as the command).
Save As → Alert, set a cron schedule, then Add Actions → ITSI Maintenance Window Management.
Keep the action parameter default_dry_run = true until you have validated the environment.
Review outcomes in the app log: index=_internal source=*itsi_maintenance_window_management.log*.

div.p: When to use which: the command for interactive/on-demand runs with inline results; the alert action for scheduled, unattended automation with a logged audit trail. Both share the same validated, idempotent engine.
Operations run as the user running the search (command) or the saved-search owner (alert action), using that principal's ephemeral session key. No credentials are stored. Three layers apply:

ol.li:
ITSI capabilities (enforced by ITSI against the session key):
read_maintenance_calendar — list / read / dry-run
write_maintenance_calendar — create / update / cancel
delete_maintenance_calendar — delete
ITSI object RBAC: you need write on the target service's team; entities use the Global/default security group. Missing access → controlled authorization_failed_403, no change.
App KV Store: your role must have read/write on the app collection itsi_mw_automation_state (idempotency/state) or writes fail with state_backend_error.

div.p: For scheduled use, the owner also needs schedule_search; own scheduled searches with a dedicated service account. Admin is not required. Example roles shipped with the app: itsi_maintenance_manager (read/create/update + KV access) and itsi_maintenance_reader (read-only). See docs/ROLES.md for a least-privilege setup.
1. Read the inline result. Every run returns per-request rows with result (success/failure/noop), error_category and error_message. Start there.
2. Application log (structured, sanitized — never contains secrets):
On-disk path: $SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/itsi_maintenance_window_management.log. Filter by a run with | search request_id="...".
3. Platform logs for REST/handler issues:
div.pre: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd (component=*Maintenance* OR maintenance_services_interface) (log_level=ERROR OR log_level=WARN)
div.p: 4. Inspect idempotency / operation state (app KV Store):

tr.td: Operation disabled by config (e.g. delete). Enable it in the alert action parameters (alert UI), or set enable_delete=true in itsi_maintenance.conf [safety] for the command.
Missing ITSI capability (read/write/delete_maintenance_calendar) or no write access to the service's team. Grant via role/team.
Your role lacks read/write on the app KV collection itsi_mw_automation_state. Use the itsi_maintenance_manager role.
The object_key is wrong. Use the ITSI object _key, not its title.
Use UTC epoch seconds (or ISO-8601 with Z/offset); end_time must be > start_time.
Same request_id reused with different data. Use a new request_id for a new change.
Exceeds a configured maximum (rows/objects/duration/horizon). Adjust in Set up if appropriate.

div.p: Where settings live: the command reads itsi_maintenance.conf [safety] (edit in local/ on self-managed Splunk, or via the configs/conf-itsi_maintenance REST endpoint on Splunk Cloud). The alert action uses its own parameters, editable in the alert configuration UI.
